findings.reason: without a sentence repointing the control at the new source (or naming a control that mutates the dispatcher registry), the node meets a red gate it was not warned about and the least-effort repair is to weaken the control, leaving the registry case unproven even as the plan claims it was made able to fail.
findings.text: the filter node is told to make the registry case "compare the views the MCP tool's schema advertises with the dispatcher's", replacing its input `mcp.CREW_TOOL_VIEWS` with the `view` Literal in `reckon/_mcp_tools.py`; but §6's declared negative control at tests/test_crew_view_serves_every_view.py:236-240 monkeypatches `mcp.CREW_TOOL_VIEWS` and asserts that the same registry case raises, so after the prescribed change the control asserts on an input the registry case no longer reads and the control itself fails — while the plan names no replacement control for the registry change (its filter-node control at plan.html:339 only drops `--mine`)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited path resolves, including the foreign guide `imas-ambix ops/lane-cycle/AGENTS.md:40` and the correction that `skills/reckon-build/scripts/worktree_fleet.py` reads live pointers rather than calling `crew directory`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the filter node changes the registry case's source of truth to the MCP schema, which stops §6's declared control (`tests/test_crew_view_serves_every_view.py:229-242`) from exercising it, and no replacement control is named (plan.html:325,339).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — fixtures land in `tests/test_read_verbs_retire_behind_crew_view.py` and gate logs under the repository's evidence tree; nothing is written to a session scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol or comment in the changed text; `cso-*` are node identifiers, which are the plan's own dispatch vocabulary.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause (a tautological registry comparison and a narrower-than-dispatcher schema) matches the cited code, the prescribed mechanism produces the stated counts (verified 10/19/13/6), and the invoked path is real: `_crew` (reckon/mcp.py:1936) forwards to `serve_crew_view` and is the registered `crew` tool.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each s9 node has one deliverable (retire `ledger`+`velocity`; grow the live view and reconcile the view surface; move `crew list` callers; tombstone `crew list`), and the filter node's schema/view-list/extractor work is the single "make the surfaces' declared view sets agree" goal its gate proves.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §9 depends-on s7 and s8, both resolve, and §9's nodes write `reckon/crew_run_commands.py` which §8 owns; the §5 edge into `reckon/mcp.py`/`_mcp_tools.py` is satisfied because §5 has landed, so no dependency it needs is missing.
